reviews.comment: Linear algebra isn't bad and his teaching was fine, but is hand writing is pretty impossible to read. Also he spends like 20 minutes of each class just reviewing what he went over last class, so the pacing of the class felt pretty slow until the end. Overall it's fine, you can get an A, but I was never super engaged or anything.

For an upper level math class, I thought he did a pretty good job of teaching the material. Always stops to answer questions and is very nice to students. Material gets really confusing after the 1st exam, but he grades really forgivingly and always has tests out of 120 points (so you can miss 20 and still get a 100). Curved 2nd exam to help us out

The only assignments in this class are really short homeworks and exams. (Exams are 70% of the grade) He was not the best lecturer, often got things wrong in class, and honestly his numbers and letters were outright illegible. Honestly if I could make out the numbers he was writing on the board this class would not have been as hard.

Dr. Paouris is a really smart guy and he cares about his students. His class is very test heavy but he grades quite forgivingly. However, there isn't a ton of content to prepare for the exams beyond the HW and his lectures can be a bit too theory heavy making it hard to review for the exams.

Nice guy, but definitively focuses more on proving theory rather than teach the students how to solve problems. Handwriting sucks too, so if you don't go to class then good luck trying to understand his notes. Class is graded on just homework and exams, and the exams aren't too bad, but most the stuff on his exam reviews aren't even on the test.

In my opinion, he is a good professor. He summarizes material from the previous lecture at the start of each class, which helps students understand new concepts when earlier material is needed. He also goes into proofs, which is important for understanding how linear algebra works.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely smart dude. I personally didnt go to many lectures bc 8 am and he couldnt care less if you show up. He posts notes online but not lecture recordings. 70% of grade is exams. Exams are hard, but the grading structure is generous. W prof, would take again.

Really thorough with his explanations. Each lecture, he'd review over the topics we recently covered so they were still fresh. Made and worked out study guides which were very similar to the problems on the test. Does make mistakes when working out examples somewhat often but is good about catching them himself or when pointed out.

reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
As mentioned before, his handwriting can be rough, but if you follow along with his words, you can get the gist. 

He does spend a lot of time on proofs and theorems, but pair it with the Math Center's 304 help sessions, and I could learn things well enough.

Attendance is not mandatory, but you won't want to miss a day.

His lecturers were okay. He went into proofs a lot that never showed up and didn't work out as many examples as he should've. His assignments and exams weren't horrible but they occasionally had a problem that we hadn't seen before.

Gives almost zero materials to study outside of lectures (aside from some undecipherable handwritten lecture notes). Went too much into the proofs for certain theorems, which had zero relevance on exams. Learning how to do problems mostly came from homework and exam reviews. Not horrible, but lackluster relative to other 304 profs.

He just does proofs that nobody understands. Theres not much homework which is not good since that is the only time you will see exam like material, not the proofs he wastes time doing. When he tries to do examples, they are ALWAYS wrong, and his handwriting is barely legible in the notes. How does somebody make a 1, 2, ,7 and 9 all look the same.

Hard class, it is what it is. Really smart dude and does his best to teach hard material. He could not care less if you dont come to class. Overall, I would take him again. Only thing is he doesn't post lecture recordings, but I didn't go to most classes so I can't really complain.

DONT TAKE HONORS FOR THE LOVE OF GOD
He doesn't teach any of the material that's on the exam 
He messes up every example problem in class 
He's about to fail my entire section because not a single person has a clue how to solve the honors proofs. DO NOT TAKE.

He is a great professor. Your grade is just weekly homework, 3 exams, and a final. From what I've heard prof Paouris is the best Linear Algebra professor. He gives a ton of partial credit on exams and is pretty easy overall. The beginning of each new unit is confusing, but by the end of it you understand it pretty well. I definitely recommend him.

It's not that he's not knowledgeable about linear algebra-- however, his entire class is him writing proofs and giving little explanation of their application, or use of concrete examples. This doesn't help when the class itself is difficult material. I'm normally a straight A student and I made a 70 on the midterm. Pray for me on the final...
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Paouris is a very lackluster professor. His lectures are boring, he doesn't seem to care much, just writes proofs. I don't really learn anything in his class and have to rely on youtube to learn the material.

Homework (around 5-10 problems, never more than 12) assigned weekly and grades every problem meticulously. I had a TTH class, we had 2 exams and a final. His exams have True and False questions based on theories. His tests are very long but relatively straight forward. I always felt overwhelmed by the amount of content that was tested.
